# Check slugify with <test>
import subprocess
result = subprocess.run(
    ['python', '-c', '''
from markdown.extensions.toc import slugify
print(f"Slugify of <test>: {repr(slugify(\"<test>\", \"-\"))}")
'''],
    capture_output=True, text=True, cwd='.'
)
print("STDOUT:", result.stdout)

Now I see the issue! When I parse manually with `parseDocument(lines)`, the tree is different from when I call `convert()`. The manual parse gives `get_name` returning `` `<test>` `` (with backticks), but after full conversion, it returns `'<test>'`.

The difference is that during `convert()`, the inline processing happens BEFORE TocTreeprocessor runs. The inline processor converts the backtick-wrapped `<test>` into a `<code>` element with HTML-encoded text content.

So the original code flow is:
1. Block parsing creates h1 with text `` `<test>` ``
2. Inline processing converts to h1 > code with text `'<test>'`
3. TocTreeprocessor runs and calls `get_name(el)` which uses `itertext()` → `'<test>'`
4. But wait, my test shows `get_name` returns `` `<test>` `` in the manual parse...

Actually, looking at the output again, the manual parse gives `` `<test>` `` because the inline processing hasn't happened yet. But during `convert()`, the inline processing has already happened, so the tree has the `<code>` element.
